requirement: Parse a kubectl-style YAML file holding several documents separated by ---, rejecting unsafe tags and documents without a kind or name, and skipping empty documents.
skeleton: A ManifestError and load_manifests reading every document with safe_load_all inside a try, skipping None, and validating mapping, kind and metadata.name per document index.
caption: Loading a multi-document YAML stream of Kubernetes-style manifests with PyYAML without trusting it. ManifestError is a plain Exception. load_manifests(text) materialises yaml.safe_load_all into a list inside a try block so any yaml.YAMLError, including a rejected python tag, is raised as ManifestError saying invalid YAML chained from the original. It skips empty documents, then for each remaining one raises ManifestError naming the document index when it is not a mapping, when its kind is not a string, or when metadata is not a mapping with a non-empty name. It returns the manifests in order. The fixture asserts ordered documents with empty ones skipped, an empty stream, rejected python tags, wrapped syntax errors, the index of a list document, and the kind and metadata.name checks.

plan.intent: Read a multi-document manifest file before applying it
constraints: The generator is consumed inside the try so every yaml.YAMLError becomes ManifestError
A non-mapping document raises ManifestError with its index
Kind must be a string and metadata.name non-empty, else ManifestError

rationale.teaches: safe_load_all is lazy, so consume it inside the error handler, skip None documents, and validate each manifest's shape with its index.
rationale.why: Iterating the lazy generator outside the try leaks raw parser errors, the unsafe loader executes tags from the file, and loose shape checks crash later on list documents.

ops.docstring: Load a multi-document YAML stream of Kubernetes-style manifests safely.

ops.source:
class ManifestError(Exception):
    """Raised when a document in the stream is not a valid manifest."""

candidates.why_wrong: The unsafe loader runs python tags from the file instead of rejecting them.
A bare --- separator is reported as a non-mapping document.
A numeric kind is accepted as long as the key is present.
List metadata crashes with AttributeError instead of ManifestError.
The lazy generator escapes the try, so syntax errors are not wrapped.
